NIX Advance 10 Inch USB Digital Photo Frame - HD IPS Display, Auto-Rotate, Motion Sensor, Remote Control - Mix Photos and Videos in The Same Slideshow I purchased one of the 15" frames as a gift for an older relative. First the good: Once you set it up, it does what it needs to, even after a power outage. One not need to touch anything and the pictures will display on their own.

However, if you use shuffle, you'll only see a small portion of your total pictures. It seems to have favorites that it repeats over and over. There are different theories as to why this is in other reviews - all I know is it's a poorly designed feature. If you want to see ALL your pictures, you really need to never have it cycle off (which will shorten the lifespan - I got a 4 year warranty via squaretrade, so always on will work best for me).

Second, the pictures display fine, but the screen has a very bright edge. This is excessively noticeable on darker pictures or pictures that don't fill the whole screen due to the size. If you like a bright grey highlight on the outer edge of your pictures, then this is the frame for you! You can fix this a bit by playing with the brightness and contrast, but it's still an issue.

Good gift for people who need a "set it and forget it" device who may not even notice some picture defects, but if showing for your own high quality photos - especially night scenes, you will be disappointed.

Kindle Oasis E-reader with Leather Charging Cover - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity, Built-In Audible (Previous Generation - 8th) “I wonder how long it has been we readers have gazed at the young person sitting under a tree at night reading a book on the Kindle home screen..oh, our love affair with books and being able to read our stories late into the night…...by candlelight….anywhere.”

Pre-release technology reviewers commenting on the price of the Kindle Oasis are wrong. The new Kindle Oasis is worth the the price Amazon is charging, including cover it hardly represents at all an increase in price when compared with a Kindle Voyage with cover. Yet it provides the two most asked for improvements in mobile devices: increased battery life reducing the need to frequently recharge, and improved screen legibility (new sans-serif Ember font, and more LEDS that provide increased brightness).

“When we are immersed into the story of our favorite books, only that world matters.”

Pre-release technology reviewers have compared the Kindle as a single purpose e-reader, to multipurpose devices like in smartphones, tablets and computers. When we choose to read, we are seeking a bit of solitude in the day and night. Oh, how easy it is to remember being annoyed with yet another incoming phone call, text message or email. The power of focus!

“The tactile feel of a book”

Pre-release technology reviewer have labelled the Kindle as luxurious with it’s leather cover. How soon we forget our books covered with leather! And we are willing to pay an extra price for it!

As I sit across the street from the one and only Amazon retail store “in the world”, I have unboxed and set up my new Kindle Oasis. Maybe I am one of the few ordinary people outside of Amazon and the technology press in the world to have been able to purchase one so soon. The feeling reminds me of going to a release party in the same shopping center for the latest Harry Potter novel.

This Kindle is new, like the latest release from our favorite author.

It connects me to reading anywhere, late at night when there is little light.

The Kindle Oasis is magical.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader with Leather Charging Cover - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity, Built-In Audible (Previous Generation - 8th)

Macbook Pro Charger 96W Usb-C Power Adapter For Macbook Pro Air 13 14 15 16 Inch Mac Book Retina M2 M1 2022 2021 2020 2019 2018 2017 2016 Usb-C To C Fast Charging Charger For IPad Pro/All USB C Device My laptop came with a Dell PA1900-02D (9T215) which I still have and works fine. I wanted a second charger for another location. The EasyStyle SK90B195462looks like the original but is much lighter, probably due to being a switching power supply. My laptop had been discharged down to 5% prior to plugging the replacement charger in. The connector fit fine, but the laptop did not recognize the charger and warned that it may not work. I figured that's just Dell telling me it's not a Dell accessory. I permanently shut off the warning (an option) and continued to use the EasyStyle charger. Charging appeared normal and battery status was indicated as charging. However, after a short while it seemed stuck at 11% charge. I came back a few hours later and it was still indicating at 11%. I plugged in the Dell charger and 100% full charge was indicated immediately. I unplugged the Dell charger and the computer still indicated nearly full charge. I plugged in the new EasyStyle charger and the indication was charging and still near full charge.
My conclusion is that the charger works, but may cause the computer to give incorrect charge status under some conditions and it will be best to unplug the charger to get an accurate battery status.
text_fidelity_b: Macbook Pro Charger 96W Usb-C Power Adapter For Macbook Pro Air 13 14 15 16 Inch Mac Book Retina M2 M1 2022 2021 2020 2019 2018 2017 2016 Usb-C To C Fast Charging Charger For IPad Pro/All USB C Device

I think that's the next eclipse. These work great (hence four stars) but it's kind of a flawed idea.

They're too powerful. Maybe you can see some sunspots with these you'd miss with regular eclipse solar viewing glasses, but really the regular eclipse glasses work fine. I gave up on the binoculars and used those.

The fundamental problem with these is, how do you find the sun? It seems dumb, but at 8x, you spend a fair bit of time searching a perfectly black sky. You can't see anything through these EXCEPT the sun, so there are no landmarks or other things to guide you. Unless you peak at the sky and fry your eyeballs.

Plus, during the real show - totality - you can't use these at all. Nothing is visible.

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest. I really wanted to love this keyboard. In fact, I have purchased three of them over the past 18 months. If it weren't for the fact that two of them simply stopped working altogether with the steady red LED problem along with complete lack of function, I would probably have given this deice a 5 star review, and that is all of the variants that exist of this keyboard. When it works, it is a wonderful device. The problem is, there are clearly some major quality issues.

First off, what is it about this keyboard that is so fantastic that makes it so popular if it has so many problems? Answer, it feels wonderful, and when it works, it's a dream. It is the right shape and size even for practically all typically sized hands. Maybe even for some of the more tiny-handed men out there. Microsoft has perfected the bezel curve of the ergonomic keyboard in the Sculpt, and the amount of travel it gives each key is perfect. The feedback of the keys (as in the feel) is perfect as well. The apparently physical quality of the device seems well made (if though it clearly has some design flaws). Even the amount of "clack" that the keyboard makes is satisfying without being obnoxious.

So what's the problem? Aside form the things people have talked about ad nauseam (broken keys, losing that tiny transceiver means the keyboard is useless, etc.. being the seemingly biggest issues) so along with practically all of Microsoft's consumer-grade products, support is nowhere to be found. While MS offers comprehensive support plans for their corporate products, you are on your own with accessories, even if they are expensive bluetooth accessories. They don't even host proper forums for their accessories (there is no category for this on their official forum) and any information elsewhere on the internet about the Sculpt is strangely scant, so trying to find out what the steady red LED means is definitely a no-go. Anything I find is either for another model or simply doesn't map to this condition. Therefore, I can't even find out what the red LED light even means, let alone attempt to resolve the problem. Their phone and chat support offers no meaningful help as they are unfamiliar with the device. Since I have a Mac they balk and say the device isn't supported on a Mac, even though I have been using it for 9 months beforehand without incident. Also, the red LED turns on immediately after the new batteries go in so it's probably nothing to do with signal and a failure of the device itself. This seems further evident since the bottom of the keyboard that is underneath the light actually gets warm to the touch, so I should assume the keyboard is fried. This would be the second Sculpt keyboard that this has happened to in less than a year so this is not an outlier. I don't do anything to my keyboards that would kill them like this. My old Logitech Wave that I keep having to go back to keeps on ticking.

Also, note that apparently USB 3 interferes with the wireless signal between the USB dongle and the keyboard, a problem I have personally experienced when my keyboard strangely stopped receiving input temporarily for a few seconds and then resume. I thought I solved the problem by using an old USB 2 hub to get the dongle physically closer to the keyboard as I thought it was a reception issue that is so common with Bluetooth devices. (I am not even sure if this even uses Bluetooth and it might just be some proprietary RF signal.) But in fact, I later learned that it was the use of a USB 2 port that was far away from my USB 3 ports!

Sadly, as tantalizing as this device may be, I would steer clear of it. It's nothing but trouble.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Wireless Desktop Keyboard and Mouse - Black. Wireless , Comfortable, Ergonomic Keyboard and Mouse Combo with Split Design and Palm Rest.

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite Leather Case, Onyx Black - fits all Paperwhite generations prior to 2018 (Will not fit All-new Paperwhite 10th generation) After being a NOOK user for just over a year, I fell in love with the Kindle Paperwhite, decided to switch platforms, and joined the Kindle family in February. After using the Kindle for about a week without a cover, I felt I needed to protect my new device. I bought two cases from third party vendors, and they were just okay. My Paperwhite seemed to float around inside these cases, so I bit the bullet and bought Amazon's leather cover in Fuchsia. When I received it, I wasn't thrilled with the color, so I returned it and got Onyx Black instead. While I love it--it's very stylish, elegant, and the border blends perfectly with the device--my Kindle also kept blending in with other tech gadgets around the house that live in black cases. I went to Best Buy and looked at the case in Royal Purple (in my area, they only sell Onyx Black, Fuchsia, and Royal Purple), but again I didn't care for that color either. On a whim, I ordered the Persimmon case, which I got yesterday. I'm very happy!!! It is a beautiful coral color, not what the Amazon website depicts, but also not a true red, and the trim accentuates the Kindle perfectly. I don't find it distracting. I have been so happy with this case that I paid the extra $20 to turn off Special Offers and it works as advertised. The Kindle sits perfectly flush inside, closes flush, and even when I fold the front cover back there's no floating (very distracting when you're reading and the Kindle "shifts" when you move your finger to turn a page). Anyway, I'll be selling the Onyx Black case, which is, after one month of use, in excellent condition. I highly, highly recommend these cases for the Kindle Paperwhite, and if you like cheerful, bright colors, go with Persimmon. The only cons I can think of are: there should have been a teal and green option, and I wish the inside of the front cover had the Kindle logo engraved on it (don't think that's a lot to ask for the price; instead the inside logo feels like it was ironed on).
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite Leather Case, Onyx Black - fits all Paperwhite generations prior to 2018 (Will not fit All-new Paperwhite 10th generation)

text_fidelity_a:
Google Pixel Slate 12.3-Inch 2 in 1 Tablet Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 128GB, Aspect Ratio 3:2 The Pixel Slate is Google's computer of the near future. It is great for some people right now, but not for everyone. Google has had their Android tablets and Chromebooks for many years now. The Pixel Slate combines those two concepts into an evolving platform. The hardware is really great right now with great fit-and-finish, a very sharp colorful screen, very responsive touch sensors, and great sound quality. Battery life is very good (over 10 hours per charge). The software is evolving quickly. Google has already released many updates the Chrome operating system and I expect this to continue.

The main problem with the software is that the Pixel Slate is running two types of apps: Chrome browser web-apps and Android apps. The user interfaces for these two are slightly different, which can lead to user confusion. There are also interoperability problems between the two, which also leads to user confusion. For example, Android apps can share files by just clicking on the share icon. Sharing a file from a web-app to an Android app requires downloading the app to the local file system, then opening the Android app and hunting through the file system to find and open the file. Hopefully one day some kind of automatic sharing mechanism will be implemented. Another confusion is that some web-apps and Android apps have the same name and functionality, but don't work the same. For example, Amazon Kindle has both a web-app and an Android app. If I download a book in the Kindle Android app, the Kindle web-app cannot find it, so I have to remember to use the Kindle Android app.

Who should buy a Pixel Slate? Google initially announced 4 versions of this product: one with a Celeron CPU, one with a Core m3 CPU, one with a Core i5 CPU, and one with a Core i7 CPU. I have the i5 version, which is plenty fast and responsive for anything I'm trying to do (I am not a gamer).

Apparently, the performance of the Celeron version was so bad that product has been cancelled. Prices now range from $800 to $1600, not including accessories like the keyboard or stylus. Even the $800 version is a lot of money, especially when you consider that a very good Chromebook can be had for much less money and that has a built-in keyboard. I have to imagine that the only people who should consider the Pixel Slate instead of a high-end Chromebook are people who will regularly need to use this device as a lightweight tablet. At just a pound or so, the Pixel Slate's tablet mode is much lighter weight and much less bulky than any Chromebook, even those flip-over style Chromebooks. If you can't imagine life without a physical keyboard, then get yourself a good Chromebook instead of the Pixel Slate.

The physical keyboard is not included with the Pixel Slate. Amazon sells a couple of different versions, but both have flaws, as well as very high prices. For now, I'm using a Belkin USB keyboard when I'm using the Pixel Slate at my desk. When I'm on the go, I use the tablet in touch screen mode without a physical keyboard. If a better physical keyboard comes along, I'll rethink this setup.
text_fidelity_b: Google Pixel Slate 12.3-Inch 2 in 1 Tablet Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 128GB, Aspect Ratio 3:2

text_fidelity_a:
Legrand - Wiremold Cable Management Kit, Cord Organizer and Hider, Concealer, C210S Cord Cover Kit, White I'm sure they do it for shipping purposes and to appeal to homeowners without tools, but I don't like that they give you multiple short pieces instead of fewer long pieces that you could cut down to appropriate size. That just means you need more couplers; each additional coupler decreases the appeal of the final installation.

Honestly, I hate surface mounted conduit. But there are times when it is required, and in those cases better than nothing. I own my home, so of course I put all permanent links properly inside the walls, but even then, there are times when the Cat/RG/other jacks are not directly behind the furniture holding the devices that need the cables. In these cases, I prefer to mount these with screws, and then caulk and paint them into the painted baseboards so they blend in better, although they have made these with tape for truly temporary installations.

There is just one connector for an inside corner and an outside corner (on the x/z axis). And in my opinion, these are the only two you should really need, and you probably need more of them. I am never going vertical up walls with cables; I just go from the jack along the baseboard to behind the furniture...if I need more than that, I'm afraid I need to just stop being lazy and tear down a wall or something.

I get that if you are in an apartment or a rental property, you may need more flexibility with this. But in my opinion, if you can't do a proper wall-mount TV install without surface-mount conduit, then you should just use a TV stand as God intended because this is not enough to make cables acceptable in such an install (although honestly, it is better than nothing).
text_fidelity_b: Legrand - Wiremold Cable Management Kit, Cord Organizer and Hider, Concealer, C210S Cord Cover Kit, White

text_fidelity_a: Pioneer Electronics Audition Series XW_NAS3-K Docking Station for iPod (Black) I was the happy owner of the original Bose sounddock for seven years until it stopped working this November.  I thought that was a very good run.  To replace the Bose I chose the Pioneer NAS3 and waited a month for the price to drop to $220.  I like the clean design as I wasn't looking for a display nor was I looking for an alarm clock.  On first play I was not at all impressed with the muddy flat sound until I found that under the music menu on the ipod is a setting for 'speakers'.  Going into 'speakers' I can enhance the sound with the bass/treble on setting which is comparable to the ipod EQ acoustic setting.  You can really bump up the sound by turning on both but for me the sound becomes unnaturally bright and the bass distorts.  In other words the dock does respond to all ipod EQ settings.  Under 'speakers' I can also set the ipod display to always be on, always be off, or only come on when I press a key on the dock or on the remote.  Speaking of the remote, the range is strangely bad as you need to point it almost directly at the unit.  To make the NAS bluetooth capable then you'll need to buy the adaptor separately.  I don't know if it's only the Pioneer adaptor that will work but if that's the case, it's a pricey option at about $70. If this were an issue for me I would have rated the Pioneer three stars.  The sound quality here just doesn't earn it a five-star rating but I'll be keeping the unit.  If I had it to do it over again I would go with another Bose.

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm FinePix T300 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens (Black) For the non-professional photographer looking to get high-quality images in a variety of settings, this camera works great. I did a little experiment to see how it performed by taking it with me to Europe along with a much more expensive semi-professional Nikon (D3100). Here are the results:

Advantages:
-With our limited time, my camera was able to take a variety of shots (panoramic, zoom, close-up) quickly and easily while the Nikon could only take limited kinds because of the need to bring several lenses and because of the complexity (sometimes) of setting up a given shot
-Because it was small, I didn't have to lug around a big camera bag, which also had the potential of getting a little too much unwanted attention
-One feature I really enjoyed was the two simultaneous flash/no flash shot which gives you the same picture with and without flash, letting you choose later which you prefer
-Didn't need more than one lens
-With city shots of architecture, my camera fared better with its versatility

Disadvantages:
-In the mountains, the Nikon did better, capturing color and clarity/detail. In my shots, the trees looked less defined from high up. Also, his zoom lens was able to capture much more detail than my camera.
-Nature shots and portraits have slightly duller colors, missing something the other camera was able to capture
-There was slightly more blur in shots with movement with this camera

Conclusion:
For the price, this camera performed much better than I expected and was not as much of a hassle as our semi-professional camera, so for most people, this is not only going to be a better value, but less frustrating and cumbersome. For the professional, this is obviously not the best choice, but this isn't being marketed as a professional camera. This is a great family and vacation camera that everyone can use, and that still yields quality images with plenty of artistic integrity.
Great little camera, and fun to use!

**see pics for some examples of how this camera performed**
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm FinePix T300 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Izzo Swami Watch Golf GPS Overall, this is a very nice golf GPS for the price. I was a little worried about it being too complicated to use, but the manual explains all the features in reasonably good detail. I found it helpful to keep the manual with me the first couple of times I used it on the course to refer to, but after a few outings I felt comfortable using it.

I had an initial problem with the battery life in that it quit on me after about an hour of use. After leaving it in the charging cradle overnight, the next time it maintained its charge for a full afternoon's use. I've used it (and recharged it) several times since then and have had no problems, so it seems the first time was just a momentary glitch (or perhaps I didn't seat the charging cable firmly enough).

I very much like that it does not require a subscription to use, nor does it need to be tethered to a PC for the initial setup. It has a pretty extensive database of courses (Izzo says on their website that they cover 90% of the courses in the US). You can use their website to look up a course to see if it is included in the database.

Sat acquisition times is quick - took only a few minutes to get a lock and find my course the first time I used it. Acquisition time was even faster on subsequent uses. It uses a SiRF Star III receiver.

The display is clear even in sunlight, but it is a bit small for me. I don't usually have my reading glasses with me when I'm outdoors, so seeing the distance numbers took quite a bit of squinting. Granted, if you don't have aging eyes you won't find that to be a problem, but it would have been nice to have a larger display.

I also didn't find it all that comfortable to wear. It is lightweight and not too thick, but the strap was not very comfortable. Plus the greenish/yellow accent color (found on the inside of the strap and the sides of the unit) didn't appeal to me much - rather garish looking to my eye.

The warranty is only 90 days, which I think is too short given the price -- a year would be more appropriate.

But those are minor quibbles. Overall, the functionality is great - quick to acquire sats, accurate distances and straightforward to use. Considering the price of other brands, such as Garmin, this is a great value. Definitely should be on the short list if you're shopping for a golf GPS.

[As an aside, it's a real bear to the product out of the clamshell packaging. I didn't' factor that into the rating, but set aside some time to wrestle it out of the plastic jail it comes in should you buy one.]
text_fidelity_b: Izzo Swami Watch Golf GPS

text_fidelity_a:
Huion H610PRO V2 10 x 6.25 inch Graphics Tablet Drawing Tablet with 8192 Battery-Free Stylus Tilt Function, 8 Shortcut Keys, Compatible with Mac, PC or Android Mobile {Update} 8/17/14
Sorry my reviews have been up and down with thing. I love this thing when it works properly but it seems to have issues drivers.
I guess as the saying goes, if ain't broke don't try to fix it.
It was working somewhat fine with version 7 even though it lacked button assignment options.
But version 9 totally removed dual monitor and seems to have removed hot cell and express key assignments.
Not sure why they updated the Huion H610 pro drivers to v.9 but they removed beneficial configurations from the v. 7 setup. Huion???
Installing version 9 overrides version 7 but I wish it could have the set up configuration of version 7; it's missing alot.
In Windows 7 Pro (64-bit), version 9 installs in the Programs Files folder but version 7 installed in the Program Files (x86) folder.
The newer driver version 9 seems to be lacking a lot of the other features in the configuration set up compared to the older driver, version 7.
Version 9 lacks dual monitor support but added keyboard stroke assignments to the stylus buttons; although it is still quite limited - can't do combination strokes.
Driver version 7 supports dual monitor but lacks stylus "button" assignment which only supports "mouse clicks" but no keyboard stroke commands.

[Update] 1/28/14
Had issues initially but raised my review score from my previous disappointed one. Huion seems dedicated to make a quality product and listen to their customers. The new drivers that they literally just uploaded after I wrote them, seemed to correct the issues with pressure sensitivity not working and I didn't notice any other issues offhand. Although, there was a weird glitch when using dual monitor; when I opened up an internet browser it would not recognize the pen until I dragged Photoshop into the same screen that the internet browser was opened up in....then the stylus would recognize.
So after using it a while, pressure sensitivity curve easily bests any Wacom. Slow or unsteady strokes can display jittery in Photoshop but even Wacom's can be... so not a huge issue. Programs like Paint Tool Sai, Autodesk Sketchbook Pro and even Zbrush have "lazy mouse" features that help smooth out strokes anyways. But if you prefer to use Photoshop still, a plug-in called Lazy Nezumi may be a good alternative that "hooks" alongside most art programs ... it can smooth out your strokes as well as more customizable stroke options.
-----------------------------------

After reading the positive and negative reviews of the H610 tablets by Huion, I decided to jump on the hype and try the latest H610 Pro.
Alot of the positives reviews seemed like they were actually people who were able to get it to work properly for the most part but alot of the negatives were the people who could barely get it to work. Well, unfortunately it seems that I am one of the latter so far. I tried it on two computers (my laptop and desktop) both running Windows 7 pro 64 bit. I did my research reading forums and issues and responses from Huion before plugging it in and before installing the latest H610 PRO drivers from their website.
I made sure to uninstall any tablet drivers (wacom, windows, etc). I even disabled Tablet PC in services and even the Flicks Pen Input feature (which was recommended by Frenden). I don't have any special mods for tablets or devices installed either. I'm surprised they don't mention this in their instructions because I've read that taking these preliminary steps has helped other get theirs to work. Anyways, after doing all this disabling and uninstalling, I rebooted the computer and then installed the H610 pro drivers straight from their website.

I first tried plugging it in my laptop. It recognized the tablet which was good so far. But as soon as I launched Photoshop CS6 (64 bit) I noticed immediately that the pressure sensitivity setting had the "hazard" icon next to it which meant it most likely wasn't going to work. Any painting had no pressure sensitivity at all. One thing to note: the pressure sensitivity feature seemed to only work in the settings configuration for the Huion tablet from "system tray" icon - which was a common issue I read.

After reading some other Huion tips, I decided to try it on my other computer. I did the whole shebang of uninstalling tablet drivers and disabling previous tablet related stuff, rebooted, installed the Huion H610 Pro drivers....took forever this time as it was searching for possible updated drivers thru windows. There was an option to skip the search, so I skipped the windows update search. It finally found the Huion H610 Pro drivers and installed them. After it was installed the tablet didn't work on the desktop screen at first. The green light lit up every time I pressed down the pen but it didn't translate onscreen. So I navigated with my mouse to launch Photoshop CS6 (64 bit). Not sure if it was coincidence, but the pen actually picked up after Photoshop launched....but only for a bit until it didn't recognize it again. Pressure sensitivity was working though and finally got some movement again when I moved my mouse and then the pen. But then a few seconds later it would randomly disconnect or un-recognize the pen whether or not I moved the mouse. So I gave up. If this supposedly amazing Wacom alternative wasn't going to work with Photoshop (and most likely most other digital painting programs) then it would be pretty much useless. I've read that Photoshop is basically "plug n play" with pressure sensitivity, so seeing it incapable to turn on pressure sensitivity just pissed me off.

I also want to mention, I'm no slouch when it comes to tech because I have been building and troubleshooting computers and have used Wacom Intuous 2-4 having been a digital artist for over 15 years. I've had no issues with drivers nor any noticeable sensitivity issues that have affected my work with any Wacom... that put me to the point of frustration as easily as this Huion H610 Pro did. This is most likely a software or driver issue that supposedly Huion has been addressing for a while now (from the evidence of all the reports of people having similar issues). But it could be hardware related as well; with the pen or tablet acting up. I understand that this is a Wacom alternative and I'm not looking to get ultimate perfection from a device that is a fraction of the cost. But after reading reviews of this as being one of the best Wacom Intuos alternatives out there....my first impressions are very disappointing. I'm sure the hardware and results could be awesome once I could get one to work properly and consistently. The pressure sensitivity did look smooth when I got it to work and I can see how the pressure sensitivity curve could be better than a Wacom. Maybe Huion is known for making good hardware but lack a bunch in the software and drivers department, vice versa or both. Nobody is perfect. But an issue like this that has been lingering for a year or so in forums and reviews; seems like they aren't making much progress in a fix...especially for Windows 7. I'm not hating....just telling it like it is.

So please Huion, or anyone with similar problems, if there is a solution out there or I did something wrong, I would like to get this Huion tablet working so I could find it reasonable to sell my Wacom Intuos too....thus giving it a better rating. I going to try to uninstall and reinstall the Huion drivers as I've read others do but it's frustrating to do all this crap just to install a USB tablet. I did a clean install by uninstalling and disabling any other thing tablet related before I plugged in the tablet. I'm not sure how others got theirs to work. I'm no slouch in the computer troubleshooting department either. Sure it's a fraction of the cost of a Wacoms but all these detours you have to take to try to get the Huion to work is ridiculous...and then it still doesn't work properly. In the meantime, the Huion H610 Pro will get this low scoring review.
text_fidelity_b: Huion H610PRO V2 10 x 6.25 inch Graphics Tablet Drawing Tablet with 8192 Battery-Free Stylus Tilt Function, 8 Shortcut Keys, Compatible with Mac, PC or Android Mobile

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire E 15 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, 8th Gen Intel Core i5-8250U, GeForce MX150, 8GB RAM Memory, 256GB SSD, E5-576G-5762 I am not a gamer, nor do I have 50 internet windows open at once.
I will run between 3-7 programs at once but only 1-2 use much power.
The computer is HEAVY! not for traveling with but it does have a great battery compared to other laptops I have owned. I like the lighted keyboard as I work in the dark often while my husband is watching movies. Some users are bothered by the short light-up time but I am not bothered by tapping a random key to light it up again.
What does bother me, is that I can not allow the computer to go to sleep or close the lid without the fear of the screen not turning back on. The keyboard will light up and the power lights are on but my screen goes black. This issue began shortly before the one-year factory warranty which happened to be right when businesses were closing their doors due to COVID, so it was impossible to talk to anyone in customer service.
When I filed the complaint I received an automated response with very little detail and an address to ship my computer too. Like most others, I need my computer every day and I had no idea how long to expect the computer to be gone for shipping both ways and repair. I also worried they would not see the issue as it wasn't happening too often at first and seems very random. I did not send my laptop. Now the issue happens a lot more and I go to extremes to prevent it from sleeping.
Lesson learned, I will buy all future computers from local stores where my warranty can be handled without shipping mycomputer away for an undetermined amount of time.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire E 15 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, 8th Gen Intel Core i5-8250U, GeForce MX150, 8GB RAM Memory, 256GB SSD, E5-576G-5762

Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate I originally requested this product to review as the wireless card my newer laptop had broken and the wi-fi usb adapter I had didn't seem very fast. Then that laptop got completely broken. I am now using my older laptop that has a wireless card that works. So I thought I would try this anyway and see what happened.
The adapter comes with a CD for set up. You must have a CD_ROM drive to use this. It is very easy just click a few things and it installs in just a few minutes. And this really does make a difference. My internet is so much faster with this. There are a couple a websites I use that can take longer to load. But with this Belkin adapter, everything is much faster. I don't do any gaming but I do stream a lot of videos. They load faster now.
The only thing I don't like is that the adapter is about 2" long and 1" wide. It is much larger than the other adapter I have but that is probably why it works so much faster.
My wi-fi signal is stronger than it used to be in areas furthest from my router.
My router is Belkin as well. The box states this will work with all router brands but specifically lists these: Belkin, Netgear, Apple, D-Link, TENDnet, and TP-Link.
This seems like a good deal for the price, I really am loving the speed!

FYI: after awhile the blue blinking light from the adapter can me annoying, it is kind of bright. You might want to cover that with some dark tape.

update 8/29/14- this hasn't been working as well in the past few days, there stopped being a difference when I add it to my laptop. I'm disappointed.

text_fidelity_a:
Motorola CommandOne Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging One of the most important attributes for a headset is comfort. I've tried a few over the years, but always have found them to be a pain (literally!) if they are worn for more than 20 minutes or so. I'm very happy to report that the Moto is a dream when it comes to comfort - had it on for a three+ hour drive, and didn't even know it was there. Plus, it didn't cause a problem with my glasses, unlike other models I've tried.

Set up was very straightforward - basically just follow the prompts and it works. I didn't try out the text-to-voice feature but it sounds interesting. Not really something I would use since I don't text much at all, but if you're text-heavy, that feature would certainly be of value.

Audio quality was excellent. Had no problems hearing callers even with music playing in the car. Range was also very good.

My complaints are two-fold. First a minor one - this comes packed in what I would consider to be wasteful packaging. Looks impressive in a clear, thick plastic box, but the amount of materials used for packing is unnecessary. I did not, however, deduct anything from its rating due to that.

What did cause a loss of one star was the mic pickup. In a quiet environment it was fine. But, in a noisy environment (such as outside, in a crowded restaurant or with moderate-level music playing in the car), it picks up so much background noise that people had problems hearing me. To ensure this was actually the case, I loaned it to a friend and had him call me so I could hear for myself. It seems that the mic is either way too sensitive or not sufficiently directional - it truly is hard to hear the person's voice when they are using the headset should they be in anything other than a pretty quiet environment..

But, that aside, this is the best headset I've used to date. Especially recommended if you have had comfort issues with other headsets or are a glasses wearer.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola CommandOne Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging

text_fidelity_a:
Canon 2562A002 EF 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 is USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras The Canon 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 lens with Image Stabilization is a very capable, and more importantly, affordable lens,and is perfect for times when you just want to have one lens on the camera but you also want to have a lot of options with your focal range. While you get the benefits of a slight wide to telephoto range in one handy package, you do lose in light stops as you move through the focal range (the maximum aperture stops down as you move toward the telephoto end of the range). This is where the image stabilization comes in very handy, and allows you to keep hand shake at bay even when you have to compromise on shutter speed to get the correct exposure.

I've had no complaints about the optical quality, I think you'll be pleased with the shots you get from it - the lens may be cheap but don't confuse that with what the quality of image this lens can provide. Keep in mind on a camera with a cropped sensor (any Canon DSLR model other than the 5D and 1D models) the focal range is equivalent to @45-215mm - you lose a bit of the wide angle advantage, but you get more telephoto, so it depends which end of the focal range you value the most as to whether that is a disadvantage or not.
text_fidelity_b: Canon 2562A002 EF 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 is USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
XSories Big U-Shot Monochrome Monopod Telescoping Camera Pole 3 Feet Extension (Atlantic Blue) This is a step up from a regular monopod in that it telescopes down to a belt-hangable tool. In full extension, it's the right height to use when, say, sitting watching a performance at an event, allowing you to stabilize a phone or camera for recording comfortably. The head at the top pivots and locks into position. I like that the larger end also has a standard screw fixture that can take either the carbiner clip or be fitted to a standard tripod, which gives this a lot of flexibility. A monopod tends to be easier to move around with than a tripod.

The telescoping portions each individually lock. Getting them to lock into position so they don't slip is a little fiddly; it takes getting a feel for twisting one way or the other to loosen or tigthen and also being sure to tighten enough so it doesn't loosen on its own. On the whole, though, this is a very useful little tool. We plan to use it with our freestanding desktop camcorder to record poetry readings we're involved with so we can put them online as well as to hold our digital camera when we're out and about.
text_fidelity_b: XSories Big U-Shot Monochrome Monopod Telescoping Camera Pole 3 Feet Extension (Atlantic Blue)

I've got the back of the band tacked up with a bobby pin right now, but I'll probably wind up sewing it for a more permanent fit. I've got this band paired to my Echo, and I was able to tell Alexa to unpair; I couldn't get it to pair after I unpaired, so it may be a permanent thing. I'll have to play with it.

I bought this so I could listen to music while I'm on my treadmill in the living room, away from my Alexa Echo. And it will work great for that. That corner has perennials I don't have to deal with regularly, so that's fine with me, although I could probably get more coverage if I stuck an Alexa something in the kitchen. So this is a fantastic thing that I wasn't expecting.

So far, with the wrapping ear piece, this pair seems to stay on my ears much better than the buds that just pop into the ears. They paired easily to my iPhone and connect automatically each time I take them out of the case. The sound is decent or at least decent enough for me. I do not use these for just listening to music or videos, I have better over the ear headphones for that purpose. For me, I just use these for running, working out or maybe while working around the yard. For that purpose, the sound quality is pretty good. The only suggestion I have is remember to take the clear tape off the charging contacts; I did not realize it was there and my earbuds were not charging each time I put them back in the case. On the upside, I did learn that the battery life is excellent on these earbuds. I cannot say how long they actually lasted before I charged them, but I probably went on 5 or 6 runs before the first ear bud died. With the tape off the contacts, they do charge automatically each time they are placed back in their case. A nice feature is that the case can be charged either with a cord or by setting the case on a charging pad. The price was reasonable. I would recommend these wireless earbuds to anyone looking for a set. Since I cannot fully say how long they will last or how durable they are, I will reserve the 5th star until I have owned these for a while.

Updated 12May21: Ok, I really want to like earbuds, but I cannot. As many times as I have tried earbuds, they just always feel like they are coming out of my ears, even w/the ear wraps on these buds. Having to continuously re-seat the ear buds in my ears while running just doesn't make for a comfortable run. So, I went back to a pair of wired BT headphones; which sit in my ears much better.

ASUS ZenBook 13 Ultra-Slim Laptop, 13.3” Full HD WideView, 8th Gen Intel Core i5-8265U, 8GB LPDDR3, 512GB PCIe SSD, Backlit KB, Fingerprint, Slate Gray, Windows 10, UX331FA-AS51 This review is about what I think >90% of users will care about. The detail specs are a step further, higher and faster and advertised and advertised. The Asus ZenBook 13 has been my go-to everyday toting computer for some 7-8 years.

I have last year’s i5 gen7 ZenBook 13 to directly compare the two.

P.S. This Zen-book has been so good that I had it modified to incorpoarte medical practice compliant HIPA secured software. It's a step function increase in my nightly homework replacing my 7-year old Dell. This laptop is ubiquitously practical with 180 screen twist for descirbing patient procedures. With the med-system handshacks, its like 3x faster than the Dell.

First, this new i5 gen8 ZenBook 13 has a quarter inch all-around smaller footprint. The 1/4" is immediately noticeable from last year’s edition. The 1/4" bezel is noticeably better. As small a footprint as the two have, Asus has reduced the size with no compromise in keyboard utility.

This year's ZenBook is noticeably thinner. Recharge and headphone jack are reversed. This year's hinge is slightly more robust to account for the reduced thickness. The hinge has been a 'should improve' on ZenBooks since inception. This years may solve the issue for good.

The plug-outs are changed. Make sure the output ports are what you want. For my purposes, the addition of a standard HDMI vice last year’s mini-HDMI is an improvement requiring no adapter. Last year’s SD input has been correctly reduced to the increasingly popular/common micro-SD. Plug-out needs are easily resolved with a USB-C adapter hub.

The discrete Nvidia graphics will be an interesting exploration.

The Asus fingerprint reader has never failed. This edition looks identical to last years and has been creatively moved right and off the touchpad. The ZenBook has been the very best reader compared to my HP Envy (dang good) and Dell XPS (50:50 chance).

This year's battery is new tech. The lithium-polymer battery promises up to 14 hours and includes fast-charge technology that takes "just 49 minutes" to recharge to 60% capacity. I get 11 hours out of last year’s battery every day. I can't recall running out of battery on last years on battery save mode on trans-con flights.

Wish it came with Windows Pro instead of Home, but oh well.

Finally, both last years and this year are so fast you'd have to instrument to tell a speed difference. The ZenBooks 1-2-3 second boot to Windows is 'instant' for practical purposes.

Love it. Exceeds expectations. There's no purchase mistake to be made with the UX331.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ZenBook 13 Ultra-Slim Laptop, 13.3” Full HD WideView, 8th Gen Intel Core i5-8265U, 8GB LPDDR3, 512GB PCIe SSD, Backlit KB, Fingerprint, Slate Gray, Windows 10, UX331FA-AS51

text_fidelity_a:
Klipsch GiG Black Portable Speaker, Black I really wanted to like this speaker. It comes complete with international plugs, an a/c wall charger, and two pouches which I assume is one for the unit and one for the accessories. It is somewhat attractive with a built-in stand that allows you to either place it on its side or in an upright position.

With most speakers, once you have paired it with your device (an Iphone 5s, in my case), you should be all done. This is not so with this unit. The speaker has a spring-loaded slide switch that you push on. It gives you a guitar confirmation tone so that you know that it's working. Now you must go to the "Settings" icon on your device and manually choose the Klipsch speaker. Then you will hear another guitar confirmation tone letting you know that it is paired. You must do this EVERY SINGLE TIME. It is ridiculous. Of course when you turn it off, it will give you yet another guitar confirmation tone.

The sound is very good, but the extra step of always having to re-enable the bluetooth connection through "Settings" totally negates anything positive about this speaker. There is absolutely no reason why my Sony SRSX5 and my JBL Charge automatically pair with my device whenever I turn them on, and yet this one does not. I keep trying to understand why the developers came up with this procedure, but it totally baffles me.

I know that other users have complained in the past about charging issues. Perhaps Klipsch listened to them and fixed this problem because I have not had any difficulties with that.

If you're gonna spend money on a good speaker, please look at the Sony SRSX5. It is an outstanding speaker with logical functions and exceptional sound.
text_fidelity_b: Klipsch GiG Black Portable Speaker, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise) This is the second case I have gotten that I could not give a good rating because of the bottom part, which does not fit with the adapter (to allow older devices to work with the new iPhone), and it does not fit most professional cables that go into the headphone jack.
Because my car has a built-in charger and system that plays with i-technology (previous generations), I HAVE to use the adapter, not just the new wire. Because I am a dancer and instructor and use my phone for job every day, I HAVE to have a case that lets me plug into our system. For those reasons, this case, like the last one I got, is useless to me.

Could you peel back the case to leave the bottom exposed? Yes. But over time, this warps the plastic and creates a loose fit, and putting it on and taking if off can cause the screen protector to come off around the edges.

Could you cut part of the bottom to allow the adapter and wires to fit? No. The plastic is thick enough that the wire will still not fit the headphone jack. As for the adapter, it might fit, but it will want to come out because the thickness, again, will make it want to separate.

So far, the only case to fit my iPhone is a pretty cheap import that has very thin plastic and is generally not a great case either. Is it a design problem with the phone as well? Maybe, but the people making cases should take that into account and design something that works with the iPhone 5 as it is, not as we wish it were. I guess I'm keeping my brand X case a bit longer.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 1350LMT 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)) I drive in and around the Boston area, where none of the streets run north/south or east/west, every other intersection is a rotary, and a wrong turn down a one way street can take you an hour to correct.

The Nuvi is slightly better than trying to drive with a map on your steering wheel. I have been using mine for awhile now, and it mostly gets me where I want to go.

The problem is mostly how it does it. As many have already noted, there is no easy way to get it to show you alternate routes. And out of the city, especially, the route it gives you can be full of surprises. Take you off the highway and onto a dirt road for no reason whatsoever surprises. That happened to my husband on his way to a job in Hartford.

And forget trying to get around traffic. I was using it to get home from a doctor's office and saw that there was a ton of traffic on the route it was giving me through Harvard Square, so I turned toward another way home - one I do not know as well, but I know it is possible to get home that way - expecting the Nuvi to tell me it was recalculating and give me my next turn.

It did so, and I turned and followed the directions each time as it - get this - took me into the Harvard Business School parking lot and then out onto a one way street that put me on a no-turning-back 100% committed course to the traffic in Harvard Square.

Thanks, Nuvi.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 1350LMT 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer))

Canon PowerShot SX500 IS 16.0 MP Digital Camera with 30x Wide-Angle Optical Image Stabilized Zoom and 3.0-Inch LCD (Black) (OLD MODEL) I recently took this camera, along with my PowerShot Elph 110, on a Caribbean cruise. Because I have the waterproof case for the 110, I used it whenever I was shooting in wet areas and also for underwater shots. I used the SX500 in dry locations. In some instances, I was able to take comparable shots with both cameras and the difference was really striking. Let me preface this by saying that I'm NOT a photographer. I'm just someone who likes to take a lot of pictures. I like them to come out well, but I know virtually nothing about photography beyond what I've learned through trial and error.

I found the low-light shots taken with the SX500 to be FAR superior than those taken with the Elph. Yes, it's difficult to capture a moving subject in low light. This isn't and expensive, professional camera. I'm very pleased with the results considering the price I paid.

The biggest selling feature was the zoom lens. I was absolutely AMAZED how clear shots taken from VERY far away came out. I took this camera to Opening Day, to see the Red Sox players get their World Series rings. We didn't have the best of seats, so I had to really max out the zoom lens. I was certain the photos would be blurry. It's difficult to hold a camera really still, extremely zoomed in, while standing in a crowd. The photos were OUTSTANDING. I mean really...outstanding!

I'm extremely pleased with this purchase. The camera is small and easy to carry with the strap around my neck. When I want something I can slip in my pocket, I opt for the Elph.

I would classify this as a bridge camera. It's NOT as easy to carry around as a pocket-sized digital, but it's also not as cumbersome to carry around as a more professional model. It's EASY to use...even for novices like me! And it takes great photos. I'm sure as I have more trial-and-error lessons under my belt, my shots will be even better.
text_fidelity_b: Canon PowerShot SX500 IS 16.0 MP Digital Camera with 30x Wide-Angle Optical Image Stabilized Zoom and 3.0-Inch LCD (Black) (OLD MODEL)

Plantronics BackBeat PRO Wireless Noise Canceling Hi-Fi Headphones with Mic - Compatible with iPhone, iPad, Android, and Other Smart Devices I would, that I could give these headphones a zero-star rating. As I don’t think they deserve a whole star. When I was in school, a gold star meant something. And these headphones are not deserving of such.
Ok, on with the bad. My first set of these. If I would whipe the sweat out of my left ear. Left ear specifically, as the right ear did not produce this effect. The sound would cut off. Not the little off, then on again. As the phones shut off when you take them off your head. So a little off then on, would be expected. But I mean off, and stay that way. Then you need to turn off the headphones, with the switch, and back on again.
Which leads to the second problem. The phones cannot reconnect after the connection has been broken. The computer will blue screen, and restart. I thought, well maybe it is the Bluetooth receiver. So I got a new one, by a different company. Same issue.
Problem three. None of the buttons work. The buttons I am referring to are the play, pause, track forward, or track backward.
And it really makes me sad, to say these bad things about these phones. And I really tried to blame something other things at fault, to save their face. Because they have the most awesome form factor I can find in a headphone. The buttons are so intuitively placed, even if they do not work. The design, is obviously a different department. And the volume, is not controlled by a buttons. But rather a good old analog type knob. And the sound quality is pretty good, and also the noise cancelling works.
Oh yeah, I almost forgot. Because I really like the form factor. I thought I should give them another chance. So I replaced this set, with another set of the same model. And had the same problems. Evey, single, one, of them.

text_fidelity_a:
BAOFENG BF-F8HP (UV-5R 3rd Gen) 8-Watt Dual Band Two-Way Radio (136-174MHz VHF & 400-520MHz UHF) Includes Full Kit with Large Battery Received as a Christmas gift. As I am not a licensed ham yet I have not transmitted on the radio, so I can't speak about any transmission issues that others may have experienced. To date I have only used it to monitor ham radio bands to understand how hams communicate.

For an affordable introductory ham radio, Baofeng radios are a good choice. Some ham "purists" seem to have nothing good to say about them, but many hams are welcoming of new operators and understand that these radios have the potential to expand the hobby.

The radio comes with a decent book (when ordered from BAOFENG TECH). There are also quite a few resources and videos online to assist in usage.

I found programming of stations to be fairly simple although a bit time consuming. There isn't really that much to it. If you are going to program in multiple channels or set offsets for repeater use then a programming cable would be a good investment. The programming cable also allows you to name individual channels.

There are some potential issues that can occur with use of this radio.

1. This radio covers VHF and UHF ham bands but also conflicts with police bands, city maintenance, and private corporation radio frequencies. There is the potential to accidentally transmit on an unauthorized band.

2. While this radio will scan UHF/VHF police, fire and EMT bands most have shifted to a new system. Some agencies are on the older systems and some simulcast on UHF/VHF but in general if you are planning on using this as a police scanner you probably aren't going to hear much.

3. There is no way to lock out the transmit key, so it is easy to press it while handling the radio if not paying attention.

As a monitoring radio the battery seems to last forever. If you are planning on transmitting a lot then an extra battery or 12VDC adapter may be warranted.

So far I really don't have anything negative to say. Good introductory radio.
text_fidelity_b: BAOFENG BF-F8HP (UV-5R 3rd Gen) 8-Watt Dual Band Two-Way Radio (136-174MHz VHF & 400-520MHz UHF) Includes Full Kit with Large Battery

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver I returned these because of a software bug with ANC - and also because the call quality was terrible.

These phones stood out for being wireless with active noise cancellation (ANC) AND pass through (so you can hear ambient sounds for safety in the City). Unfortunately, those features are the weak points of the headphones - to the point that I found I would never use the pass through and often didn't bother with the ANC.

SOUND QUALITY: VERY GOOD - EXCEPT - they tend to exaggerate the mid base a little which can make vocals - especially male vocals sound a little unclear. Listening to the same music on speakers vs the headphones, it was just plane more real sounding and pleasant on good speakers. High standard, I know. Other headphones don't have that particular problem (though may have others - like weak bass or sibilant highs). I haven't heard that many competing models, so I don't know how they compare to sennheiser or bose or anyone else in the same price class. At least others have an app with equalization (Jabra, Jaybird).

Bug w. ANC: Sometimes it would say it's on when it's off and vice-versa.

ANNOYING THING: When you engage the pass-through, it has a voice prompt that tells you the pass through is engaged. Since often I switch on the pass through when it's important to hear something, the several seconds it takes to make its silly announcement means I miss part of what I was trying to hear! I found I would always just yank one plug out of my ear instead and get the instant feedback. ALSO - this thing takes FOREVER to turn off. You have to hold hold hold and finally it announces it's powering off. Combined with poor power indicator light - this is just annoying.

NOTE: This is not a defect, but just poor design... There is NO WAY to activate Google Assistant or Siri with These. Even my cheapo earbuds let you use one of the buttons to summon Google. Without that, how are you supposed to make voice calls? I have to pull out my phone to make calls. Foo.

Combined with atrocious call quality (I could hear them, but the person on the other end is always mishearing words or saying WHAT? WHAT?), these are DOA for me.

ONE LAST THING: The APP is garbage. Just pointless.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver

Logitech HD Webcam C525, Portable HD 720p Video Calling with Autofocus - Black [[VIDEOID:132a9e1a9608d7ddcfd6e870320f72aa]] The 75 second video is intended as a supplement to the written review so that you can see for yourself how well my fairly standard computer can record 720p, and thus get an idea if your computer can benefit from a 720p recording device. This is important to consider because even the manufacturer mentions that many computers cannot keep up with the recording. I mention my system specs in the video.

It's a well designed webcam. It is very small, and the ability to protect its own lens is great. They supply ~5 ft. cord that - wrapped up - takes up about as much room as the camera itself, which allows a connection between a desktop and a separate monitor. Better would have been if they used a standard micro USB connector or some kind of cord wrap system to keep all that out of your way and allow you to use a 30cm cord for connection to your laptop.

The actual optics seem great and the autofocus works pretty well. Even Win XP SP2 allowed me to use the camera function (no video) immediately without installing any software. The software that comes with it eats up nearly 300MB of ROM (that includes their own calling application and editing software that you don't need to install) and only tries caducously to take over your computer (a registry edit and startup menu delete gets rid of unwanted reminders and useless junk running in the background). Oh...I noticed one typo in their software, which is unacceptable, and it also keeps telling me that it doesn't recognize the mic (which is built into the camera), but it records sound anyway.

The design allows for mounting on a monitor 26mm thick or less, but I suppose you could sort of lay it on top of a CRT monitor with no problems. It also allows for a fairly stable mounting on a laptop.

Great device that I would recommend, but I had to take off a star for less than perfect portability and some software blips.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech HD Webcam C525, Portable HD 720p Video Calling with Autofocus - Black

I have a smartphone, but it's getting harder for me to read on it. I have an iPad Air, but even that can be a little big on a cramped plane ride.

Plus, I sold my other seven inch tablets (a Galaxy and a MeMo), and I miss them. They're the perfect size for reading. This tablet is so much nicer than what I would have been willing to deal with for fifty bucks. However, there are a couple of issues that keep this from being a five star device, even at this price.

The first is that using an sd card to hold content is no easier than it is with the older tech media players I have spent a fair amount of time trying to figure out. If you can download it to your computer, you can put it on the card and then load the card into the Kindle, but the Kindle doesn't treat the card like a drive that you can save to. A firmware update could fix this.

The second is the weight. I'm actually not sure how I feel about this one. It's definitely heavier than I expected. But it feels solid. So, maybe I like it?

Everything else is great for what I am using it for. Reading books. Very light web browsing. Playing with my FireTV. Buying music to play on the Echo. In other words, it's a great tool for accessing the Amazonverse. As a regular tablet? Good for the price.

The cameras were purchased to help us get our pre teen back on track. He recently got himself in trouble and we set these cameras up all over the house and eventually outside to keep our child honest.

Not only did it turn our sons behavior right around, but we now have an awesome setup to monitor our house when we are not around.

Although the software was not exactly very explanatory, I will pass along some of our learnings.

The software occasionally fails to give updates on alarms but resetting the phone seems to fix this right away. You do not have to purchase their cloud software to view the cameras: just plug an HDMI cable into the NVR and a mouse and you are set to view all the motion detections and recordings. I like how the cameras are not 1080p but are 720p. This gives our 500gb hard drive a break and we can record over a month on the NVR before overwriting data.

The NVR software was easy you setup and runs completely off of the device. The cameras were easy to setup and were plug and play.

I will eventually setup my router to port forward so I can remote into the recordings at any time although I don't think that will be necessary for our needs. I love the free alerts and its great to get the notifications on the phone to alert you of motion detected!

All in all this product was fantastic for what we needed and you can not beat the bundle price for the 500gb hard drove and 8 cameras! Thanks!

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon D5000 12.3 MP DX Digital SLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6G VR Lens and 2.7-inch Vari-angle LCD My D5000 was delivered yesterday evening while I was at work. The lovely wife opened the box enough to pull the battery out and charge it for me. After a grueling 12 hour shift at work I had forgotten about my new toy.

I had purchased the D5000 w/ 18/55 kit lens then separately purchased a 55/200 VR kit lens. It was cheaper that way. Go figure.

After many doggie slobbers when I arrived home I noticed the D5000 box on the kitchen table. My heart started palpating. I tried to control my self to no avail. My new toy was here! I carefully unpacked everything. I actually followed the quick start guide and was ready in no time.

I'm a big guy with the requisite big hands. The D5000 felt good in my hands. Not too heavy, not too light. The black body was finished with a slightly rough tactile coating. Very nice. My right thumb fit nicely in the thumb spot while my right index finger felt at home on the shutter. With a firm grip on the D5000 I was able to fully articulate my wrist and point the camera in a variety of positions. The camera felt good in my hand. I could tell that I could lug this beauty around for a full day and not get the dreaded "photog's wrist syndrome."

I attached the 18/55 kit lens. The lens seemed to provide a better balance when attached to the body. The VR switch, on the lens, was factory set to OFF. My first few images didn't utilize the VR. I was so excited and getting more excited by the minute that I forgot the properly look at the lens. I could notice the difference between the VR switching. This 18/55 kit lens is quite amazing. Sure it's made out of plastic, but it does a great job. If you don't already have Nikon lenses then the 18/55 kit lens is a no brainer. Well worth it.
As the quick guide said...Frame your first subject...then BAM!

I was looking for subjects to shoot. Since I work nights everyone, except the dog, was asleep. So I can't run around flipping light switches, move knick-knacks, or anything that could involve waking the baby. God forbid I wake the baby. My wife would have my testicles drawn and quartered within 7.9 seconds. Of course it's been raining for 2 days straight. So I'm stuck in the house...with a new camera. No worries!

I really like the D5000. Coming from the "superzoom point & shoot world" this is a welcome, although a little scary, change. I used film SLR cameras up until the late 90's so I have some experience with SLR photography. But the digital advances sure make everything so much easier. I'm not a "all manual all the time" kind of guy. Like most of us, I want the added feature of full-manual to play with, but like having an excellent and fast AUTO feature. I like to spend time with my family when we're all out and about and don't like to fiddle with any settings. The family gives me plenty of time, on my own, to experiment.

I added some images above.
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D5000 12.3 MP DX Digital SLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6G VR Lens and 2.7-inch Vari-angle LCD

text_fidelity_a:
Contour +2 - Old Packaging (Discontinued by Manufacturer) UPDATE: Local retailer slashed prices and a buddy bought a new +2 (new packaging) and found : new packaging doesn't come with HDMI cable, or the external mic adaptor. He promptly returned it and got an "old packaging" and now had all the equipment. Why the "new packaging" costs more than the "old packaging" is beyond me. The "new packaging" mimics the Roam2 packaging, with no see thru "bubble" at the top of the box - BEWARE!!!

FYI - BB discontinuing the Contour line and the mounts are all 50% off, and the camera(s) are $100 off.

This is a dual review, as I own both the Contour + 2 and the Contour Roam2. I don't work for nor do I have any affiliation with Contour. I've had the Roam2 for more than 6 months, but held off writing this review until I had the +2 to compare it to. Although I don't own a GoPro, several friends do and I do their video editing so I'll chime in on the Contour vs. GoPro at the end.

MOUNTS:
Contour uses the same proprietary mounts across their lineup, so interchangeability between the two should be fairly easy (but doesn't always work out that way). I've found some to be flimsy(hat mount), while others are damn near bomb proof(suction cup)! The rotating lens means you can mount it in just about any position, however it is difficult to know that you've framed the shot with the correct orientation! Had an important video recorded upside down - laser level only lets you know it's level, not if it's upside down! One of the best features I've found is the ¼ by 20 thread on the bottom of the Contour, pretty much universal to all modern cameras and there's a TON of mounts out there reasonably priced.

SOFTWARE:
The Storyteller program needs to be installed on your computer and is fairly easy to use, but not intuitive, you need to play around a bit before you can figure everything out. The editing ability is extremely limited. (I use imovie). Software is free, and although you can use the camera(s) without first updating I suggest you do that first! The +2 also has an app that I use on my iPhone 5 - it too is free and pretty easy to use - but not as capable as the Storyteller program. The downside is you HAVE to use the Storyteller program to change settings on the Roam2, AND you have to use it if you want to use any of the GPS data with the +2.

ROAM2:
Got this for Xmas last year and immediately swapped the included 4GB micro SD for a 16GB. SUPER easy to use - charge, point, and slide the slider to the on position. Video quality is good, first few outings I had it set for 1080@30 and was very happy. In editing I found one clip I had to slow down and was slightly disappointed at the quality - since then I've got it set for 720@60 and haven't had any issues - video quality is still good (even in slow mo). Low light does induce more "noise" to the video, but if there's ambient light (streetlights etc.) you can still get decent vids. Sound quality isn't all that, it's usable, but in high winds or at speed - forget it. Battery life is really good at around 2 hours. The camera itself is very well built, one of my first uses it got throw (by an idiot) about 8ft into about 4 inches of water over concrete - few scratches, but still kept recording. This led me to look for something to help protect the aluminum body - Glock Tape, works amazing, adds some protection, but most importantly gives it some GRIP!

[[ASIN:B00C7WXTJS 6-Pack Glock Grip Tape - Pistol Grip Tape. * Use on handguns and rifles * Not gritty like sandpaper or skateboard tape. * Does not scuff clothing, holsters, furniture or car seats like those sandy tapes. * Makes chambering a round easier for arthritis s...]]

CONTOUR +2:
Only had it for a week or so, really wanted it due to the Bluetooth (to help frame shots) and was wanted the waterproof housing (worried about watersports damage on an upcoming trip) the GPS would be a plus. Once again amazing build quality - this things tough as nails. First thing I did was hook up to Storyteller and get the latest firmware update - less than 5 minutes later I was off and running! Pairing the Bluetooth took a couple of attempts, but once connected has excellent range (20 or so feet with obstructions - close to 50ft line of sight!). Using the app you can check status of battery, GPS, and memory as well as change settings and start stop recording - wish you could watch videos but oh well. The app has about a one second delay between what the camera "sees" and what you see on your phone - pretty amazing! Attached to my suction cup mount and went for a drive - took about 30 seconds for the GPS to lock on the first time (since then it only takes maybe 5 seconds). GPS is accurate. The video quality is great! Uploaded vid into storyteller and the GPS data was also great - until I exported it then there was a lag of about 5 seconds between the data being displayed and the video. Waterproof housing is bulky, yet seems a bit flimsy - still not sure it could survive 200 ft of water. Came with HDMI to hook up to TV - works really well. Haven't used the mic adaptor yet. Battery life seems to be around 1.5 hours, but spare batteries are cheap.

[[ASIN:B007PUC1UU Wasabi Power Battery and Charger Kit for Contour 2350, 2450, 2900, C010410K and ContourHD, ContourGPS, Contour+, Contour+2]]

COMPARISON:
Even though the video specs are the same between the +2 and the Roam2, the video quality of the +2 is noticeably better - even in low light. Sound quality on both suffers in high winds or speed. They both have the proprietary T-rail mounts on both sides, but the ¼ by 20 thread is about an inch further back on the +2. The Roam2 is waterproof without housing to about 3ft, but the +2 has the waterproof housing. The +2 also allows for filming while charging. The +2 has the HDMI out, as well as a jack for external mic. The +2 has the Bluetooth app, plus GPS - that combined with replaceable batteries and the better video make it worth the extra money.

CONTOUR vs. GOPRO:
I absolutely love the form factor and the mounting options available for the Contours. The Contour line has their own proprietary mounts, but the ability to use the ¼ by 20 thread mounts for other cameras (even the GoPro mounts) plus the rotating lens means there's just more ways to mount the Contour. That being said the GoPro Hero3 flat out destroys the video quality of the Roam2, and slightly edges out the +2. Of course this difference (even over the Roam2) is completely removed once video is uploaded to Youtube or other sharing sites as they compress the video during upload! I've yet to see a GoProH3 recording 1080 go for more than 75 minutes. Sound quality between all three is about the same. The GoProH3 app uses wifi - and has about a 3-4 second delay - still works for framing shots, but not much else. The GoPro also has the advantage in that you can change settings in camera - but it is a complicated affair(the +2 only allows you to choose between two predetermined settings). GoProH3 doesn't have GPS, or rotating lense. Contour recently lowered the price on the +2 it's now $50 cheaper than the GoProH3. Also it seems they changed pricing on their mounts - I went with the Contour line because of the simplicity of their system, more mounts, cheaper price, and the form factor. Now that they're cheaper it's a no brainer.
text_fidelity_b: Contour +2 - Old Packaging (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) The new Kindle arrived within 2 days of my order. I sat down and played around with it for a few minutes and learned the icons but that's all that can be done until it is registered with Amazon. I took it to Toyota while getting my car serviced. Our local Toyota dealer has free WiFi for customers. The Kindle found the hot spot and Amazon recognized the Kindle right away.  It took a few taps around the screen to get started but was easy with a little exploring. Within the time to get an oil change, I had downloaded my ebooks from Cloud and even bought a nice app on sale.  Next I stopped by BestBuy and added a Kindle micro USB to USB cable.  The cable can be used to download ebooks from your PC when not connected to wireless.  Using free Calibre to manage the free ebooks from the Internet, enables covers and metadata for those ebooks that have none.  Calibre will also download the books to Kindle from a PC.  The Fire is great but took some thinking and patience to get it to do all the things I imagined it would do. For instance, ebooks without covers will all look alike and have no title.  This is why it is important to use Calibre for ebook management. Reading ebooks is so much better than it was 10 years ago and this is only the beginning.  The download speed is great.  The reading speed is also great.The storage space is really more than enough.  The 8 Gigabytes of memory is close to 2 warehouses of data.  I read that somewhere on Wikipedia in the middle of the night.  To put it in proportion, imagine having up to 6000 books in your home. The Kindle does not get hot like a netbook and is smaller and lighter too.  The battery life is much better than my 7" netbook also.  Like other customers, I would have liked the micro USB to USB cable included in the box.  3G would be great too.  The best thing about Kindle Fire is the color.  The color is as beautiful as everyone says it is.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)
