text_fidelity_a:
XBOOM Mini Portable Capsule Speaker with Rechargeable Battery and Enhanced Bass+ Resonator (Mini - Black) -1 pack I've been using an Altec Lansing iM227 (a model that is no longer produced by Altec Lansing, but comparable models are still offered) for a couple of years and have been very pleased with it. The Xboom, however, gives me much the same performance at half the size.

The sound quality of the Xboom is impressive for the size. It puts out nearly the same bass level as the iM227, which is surprising given how small it is. It does suffer a bit in the mid and upper ranges, which do not come through as clearly and sharply as the iM227. But the output is more than adequate for enjoyment.

I really like how the two halves of the speaker can be closed up and turned into a small ball that is only about 2 inches tall. Very compact so it easily fits into a bag or jacket pocket - this speaker is designed to be carried around easily. It comes with a decent cloth pouch plus a USB charge cable.

While it will work when it is in its compact mode, for best sound it needs to be unlatched so it expands to about 3 inches tall.

Unlike the iM227 it has an internal battery (the iM227 runs on 3 AAA batteries). That's both good and bad: good for ease of use and compact size; bad in case the internal battery fails, which renders the speaker useless. The Xboom has a stated run time of "up to 12 hours" according to the specs, which is pretty accurate - I got about 10 hours out of a fresh battery. Recharge time is about 2 hours.

Operation is very simple: plug in the attached cable to your device (I'm using it as a speaker for a small mp3 player), turn it on, and listen. The Xboom has a volume control, which the iM227 lacks, and an on/off switch. There's a power indicator light on the bottom of the speaker.

Unlike the iM227, the Xboom can be daisy-chained to other Xbooms for a bigger sound. I only have one, so I can't say how well that works, but it's a nice feature.

Complaints are virtually nil. If I had to come up with something, I'd say that it would be nice to have the power indicator light on the top rather than the bottom so it would be more easily visible as a reminder to power down and save battery life. Minor point, however.

While the sound quality of the Altec Lansing is better, the size and convenience of the Xboom makes it the one I'll take along with me and use more often. Very good value for the price, and I would highly recommend it.
[Sample provided for review]

Datacolor Spyder5EXPRESS – Designed for Hobbyist Photographers (S5X100) I ended up using this colorimeter to profile and calibrate my monitor. Out of the box I was not very happy with the quality of the product. You end up getting pretty much zero instruction and no manual. I had to figure it out on my own just by looking at the product. Once that annoyance was over I got to experience how terrible the default software from datacolor is.

I looked to the reviews and decided I could make the most of this purchase by using other free calibration software. I used Argyll and DispCalGUI. If you simply download DispCalGUI it will prompt you automatically to download the Argyll color libraries.

You then go into Tools->Instrument->install Argyll CMS instrument drivers...

This will download the drivers you need to run the spyder 5.

After this calibration is possible. I calibrated and it seemed to do a decent job. All in all, the calibration software looked like it was powerful--certainly better than the default.

In the end, I returned the product. I wanted something that would work without me having to go the extra mile to get it to work. At this point, with all of the extra I had to do to calibrate I still don't know if it did a good job or not.

Dimensions can be seen in the photos I have attached.

Included is the unit only.

Pros:
*Calibrates
*Decent price

Cons:
*Terrible OEM software (-2 stars)
*Setup--while not hard--is not immediately obvious. A small pamphlet would have gone a long way (-1/2 a star)

Additional Considerations:
Go for hardware that has good software calibration tools. You cant beat the two working in synergy.

Overall: 2.5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 3 stars

If you have any further questions regarding the product in my review please leave a comment below and I will get back to you as soon as possible.
text_fidelity_b: Datacolor Spyder5EXPRESS – Designed for Hobbyist Photographers (S5X100)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech C922x Pro + Logitech for Creators Litra Glow - The Ultimate Solution for a Professional Look During Video-Calls I am comparing this to a Logitech C910 HD 1080p webcam which I've been using almost daily since 2012.

I don't stream games but I stream my live DJ broadcasts. I use 4 webcams and a green screen. I use xSplit exclusively.

This C922x Pro Stream is for gamers so they can stream on Twitch or YouTube. The camera is supposed to automatically load a background removing program so you don't have to use a green screen. This special software, Personify ChromaCam, is free when have the C922. Installing is another matter entirely. Myself, like others, have older, but capable systems that cannot install this software. I checked on Personify's website and the PC requirements are: Processor: Intel 4th generation or higher Core CPU, or the AMD equivalent (Quad core AMD Phenom), OS: Windows 7, 8, 10, and Memory: 4GB+ RAM. My system, even though its 3 years old, meets all these specs but when installing I get a 'unable to install due to ABX or ADX" something.

The camera's clarity is not any better than my 4 year old C910. In fact, my C910 has Carl Zeiss, the new cam doesn't not. The colors appear washed out with too much brightness. I expected better, but the C922 regressed a bit in the lens department.

Now here's a kicker for you...you cannot, and I mean, cannot, view the camera while changing it's settings. Yes, you heard me right. Open the camera settings and you get a windowed box for changing the settings, but the webcam does not come on or is it viewable. So, am I supposed to change the settings, open the cam, close the cam, change the settings, open the cam...etc..etc?

The mount is sturdy and multi-positional. I like the added tripod adapter. At this price point there should be a privacy shield.

I had an issue getting the camera to initially turn on. The outer ring would flash but no camera picture. Then I realized that some webcams don't like being plugged into a USB hub. After adding an extension cord and plugging in directly to my PC the cam worked.

The big question...is this camera worth the $50 more than the entry level C920 series camera? For the money you get a ChromaCam program which may or may not work and you get 6 months free xSplit service. Hmmmmm...OBS, which is quite capable, is a free service.

Logitech has so many choices lately, each with increased pricing. Let's face it, it's all about the price. Do you really need your ugly mug put up in a live game? Probably not since it's going to use PC resources that would be better used for gaming. For the $50 extra you could get a couple decent games, or a new mouse, or a mouse pad, or a boat load of peanuts.

The choice is yours.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech C922x Pro + Logitech for Creators Litra Glow - The Ultimate Solution for a Professional Look During Video-Calls

Samsung Electronics 840 EVO-Series 120GB 2.5-Inch SATA III Single Unit Version Internal Solid State Drive MZ-7TE120BW As of early 2014, this is the price/value drive to get, for a home system.

Yeah there is another drive that is as good for the same money, just sort on #of reviews or rating to have it come up. But this and that one are can't miss price/speed/value drives

I have this one in a Windows 7 machine, and it's use is transparent and I don't do all those tweaks you read about and I read all about them.

If you want to keep it simple unplug all drives but the DVD, if installing that way, and the SSD drive. Install windows 7. Profit. Than do two things. Make sure disk level indexing is off (which you should be doing anyway) this is under your C: drive properties right under where it says Compress this drive to save space. The indexing shouldn't be set if you installed the way I said, but check anyway. This will not effect windows indexing (which I vote for leaving on even on a SSD drive)

Then update your drives firmware.

Don't worry about cache and indexing, super fetch and all that. Just let Win 7 set all that all up. and all that.

Don't worry about hibernate. Use hibernate if you want, or don't, but you don't need to change it since you are running on a SSD. Same with system restore if you have the room, and you like having it on, leave it on. This drive will automatically over-provision 7% of the drive so you don't need to set that.

Windows will set up your drive just fine. If you want to go research it all and make your own decisions, that's fine I did the same thing. And the above 'simple' installation was what I decided on. (I did 3 separate installations working through various options).. I have tweaks I do, but they are tweaks I do SSD or no SSD.

A lot of information about SSD drives is based on small drives and older controllers. You don't need to worry about how long your drive will last. It will last longer than you will have your computer. Look up the tests on this on the internet to understand how little of an issue this really is. A lot of what is written about SSD's is written by enthusiasts/gamers who are into tweaking systems. If, like me, you like doing this kind of research, great. Otherwise just install windows and use your drive SDD drive like any other drive.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Electronics 840 EVO-Series 120GB 2.5-Inch SATA III Single Unit Version Internal Solid State Drive MZ-7TE120BW

text_fidelity_a:
Power Strip Individual Switch, 6 Outlets Metal Heavy Duty Surge Protector 6FT Cord 15A 120V 1800W for Home Office School Garden Industrial Aquarium (Black) I very much like that each outlet on this power strip has its own switch. It allows me to cut power to something that is plugged in without having to unplug anything. The switch lights up when it's powered so you can easily spot which outlets are active. It's a very handy design.

Unfortunately, the build quality is just average. The case is decent, and the power cord is nice and stout, but the rocker switches are pretty low-end. There's a lot of play in them, and while there is a positive click when it's depressed, it has a very cheap feel. The surge protection level is very basic. I'm fine with it since I'm using this to control pumps rather than electronics, but if you're looking for good quality surge protection, 300 Joules is not going to cut it at all.

While the presence of independent switches is a great addition, taking everything into consideration puts my rating at 3 stars (average) even when accounting for the price point. There are better made power strips with independent switches at around the same price, and the limited surge protection adds little to the overall value of this.

text_fidelity_a:
MSI G Series GT70 0ND-219US 17.3-Inch Laptop (Black) PROS: Awesome as advertised! Specs and possibly even the parts blow away most high(er)-end laptops in its class...can't beat it for the price. Was debating this over the Samsung Series 7 Gamer with similar specs and both had similar reviews but MSI performed where it counted the most. Better battery, better cooling, mostly better benchmark tests. A big deciding factor for me was that the older MSI GT70 with GTX660/670 still outperformed and outfeatured the Samsung Series 7 Gamer in most of the benchmarking tests...and this next upgrade to MSI GT70 was only $1850 when I bought it...$30 more that the Samsung at the time.

CONS: My only down was with GPU drivers not the actual laptop itself. I think the drivers are so new not even the supposed "BETA" drivers will work with it. It was almost impossible to find the GTX 675m drivers. NVIDIA recommended I get the drivers from the manufacturer's site. And from what I've found there is only one that works and it is on MSI's website. For some reason when I first looked, MSI, didn't have a "notebook" category in their drivers section. It's not even on NVIDIA's site (this had nothing to do with NVIDIA's forums going down, I checked before there forums got hacked).
My reason for purchase.....
First off, I wanted to get this off my chest because I was planning to build a workstation PC (or a powerful PC) but instead switched to getting a laptop. Being that I'm not a laptop fan, I did extensive weeks of research to find the best laptop I could find for my 3d art/animation and gaming needs. Laptop have always been way overpriced and notebook parts can't even touch the PC counterpart; in terms of performance, cooling, etc. Plus, knowing that this an MSI, helped make my decision because they have a good track record of excellent PC parts. I have been building my own desktop PC's for over 10 years and know you get to enjoy the games and 3d applications the way it was meant to be. Also, I'm in the video game development field and needed a second/backup computer/desktop replacement. My current Intel Q9550/Radeon 5700 1GB/ 8GB DDR2 RAM desktop does the JOB but is getting ancient. I was really thinking about getting a workstation or high-end gaming desktop (which would obviously be way cheaper than the most expensive laptop) but after thinking about it, I liked the idea of having the convenience and portability. And, if my desktop goes belly up one day (as it has been acting up) my work flow pipeline won't take a hit. I wont have to deal with the inconvenience of being in a HOT room with 1000W powersupply... even with air conditioning.
text_fidelity_b: MSI G Series GT70 0ND-219US 17.3-Inch Laptop (Black)

The sound is good, although I do not understand why anyone wouldn't ave noise canceling turned on! That is absolutely horrible when it is not on! It amplifies and echos every single sound. Other headsets don't do this naturally, so not sure why it is even an option. BUT, I have been noticing that the battery seems to run low very quickly, and I thought it was just my imagination at first. After them being on the charger through the night last night, I only have 90% charge? That is not normal for just a couple of months! Does this mean, in the next month it will go down again? And then again? I should have stuck with LG, these off brands really disappoint sometimes. We actually have another BCS brand headset that had to be replaced once, and the second one broke very soon after replacement, so we gave up. I should have known.
